about: The register of everything PrompTugal.news could sell, one row per package: what it is, who buys it, the proposed price, who delivers it, what must exist before it goes live, and where it stands. Kept by customers@PrompTugal.dinis from Dinis Cruz's brief of 6 November 2026. Every price except the 5 pound top-up is a PROPOSAL for Dinis to set or change, anchored on public benchmarks (see monetisation-map.md, section 'Benchmarks'). Only the top-up is on sale; nothing else is live until Dinis says so. No Stripe key, secret or customer detail belongs in this file: a Stripe Payment Link address is public by design (data/billing/topup.json says so) and goes in stripe.link once Dinis has made it in Stripe.
currency_note: GBP throughout, as the reading meter does (data/billing/prices.json). Sherpa asked on 6 November whether a Lisbon, European publication should show euros: Dinis decides; changing the currency is a price edit in Stripe, not a code change.

status_values.ready: everything needed exists; waiting for Dinis's yes and a Stripe link
status_values.designed: scoped and priced here; something named in needs_before_live is missing
status_values.parked: worth keeping in the back pocket; not for now
status_values.set-aside: considered and not to be sold, with the reason

rule_of_seven: Dinis, 6 November 2026: do the first five or six as one-off jobs; when a seventh person asks for the same thing, it becomes a package with a link. A request type is promoted from 'bespoke' to a package row here at the seventh ask (counted in requests.json).

families.B: Made for you (fixed scope, fixed price, with a change policy)
families.C: Professional services packs (with partners, three sizes)
families.D: Data you can use (the graph, matched to your own list)

packages.name: Reading credit top-up
packages.what: 5 pounds of credit for the reading meter, which prices each page by kind and freshness and never blocks a page.
packages.not_included: Nothing is blocked without it; credit is kept in the reader's own browser.
open: The link's after-payment redirect still returns to newsroom.sgit.ai, not here (REALITY.md, 'Not yet done'): a link of our own in Stripe fixes it.
A static page cannot verify a payment (data/billing/topup.json, verified: false): credit is on the reader's own screen only. Fine for 5 pounds; not for anything bigger.

stripe.note: the existing public link in data/billing/topup.json

packages.name: Vault month: as many vaults as you want for a month
packages.buyer: a reader who wants to keep their schedule, notes, saved pages and personal views in an encrypted vault of their own; the people who build their own view from our data

price.basis: PROPOSAL: start small and raise it as the market shows (Dinis, 6 November 2026). The price is a Stripe setting, so raising it costs no release.

packages.what: A vault access key that works for 30 days: create and update as many vaults as you like (the pane at /account/vault.html), open on any device with a passkey.
packages.not_included: Vaults made earlier keep opening and reading after the month ends (opening needs no key); only creating and updating stops.
packages.delivered_by: the vault server's token (SG/Send, dev.send.sgraph.ai) plus a person or a small service to issue it
needs_before_live: How a key is issued after payment. A static site cannot do it. Manual first: Dinis (or a person he names) sees the payment in Stripe and sends the key; an agent never sends it (ABP R7). Automatic later: a Stripe webhook to a small function that asks the vault server for a token, and shows it on the return page; that is a server component nobody has built (owner: dev@, with Dinis's yes).
Whether the vault server's tokens can carry an expiry or a quota. Not known to this role; Dinis or the SG/Send team to say.
data/billing/vault.json access_key.status is 'not-issued': the pane already says so; it changes when a key can be had.

stripe.note: a recurring price with the Stripe customer portal switched on so buyers can cancel without writing to us

packages.name: Bigger top-ups and gifts
packages.buyer: a reader or a team that reads a lot; a company that wants to give its people credit

price.basis: PROPOSAL: a 20 pound and a 50 pound link beside the 5 pound one

packages.what: The same credit in bigger steps, with a reference for the buyer's own books.
needs_before_live: A payment check that is not the reader's own screen (see A1 open), or a limit small enough not to matter.

packages.name: Your schedule: a personal summit plan
packages.buyer: one attendee: a founder, a CISO, an investor, a journalist

price.basis: Dinis, 6 November 2026: 'for 50 quid or 500 quid ... we'll create a customized schedule for somebody'

packages.what: A schedule for the days they are at the summit (9 to 12 November), built from the programme and the graph for the person they say they are: which sessions, which stages, which companies to find, in order, with the reasons and the sources. Delivered as a page in their own vault and a calendar file. Up to three changes included.
packages.not_included: Meetings arranged for them; any contact detail; coverage of their company.
packages.delivered_by: dev.pages@ and ontologist@ (the personal-schedule pass), an agent run, a person checks and sends
needs_before_live: The personal-schedule pass (board/guidance/2026-11-06-events-variations-and-the-personal-schedule.md, section 4): personas to graph to schedule. Until it exists a schedule is made by hand from the agenda.
A vault to deliver into (A2) or a plain page.

stripe.note: quantity adjustable, so a buyer can order for a colleague

packages.name: Your delegation's schedule (the Brazil formula, for your group)
packages.buyer: a delegation, a country team, a company sending several people, an agency

price.basis: Dinis, 6 November 2026; the Brazil story is the formula (board/guidance/2026-11-06-the-brazil-story-and-story-projects.md)

packages.what: Everything that matters to that group across the days: who from the group is where, the companies and sessions that touch them, a schedule per person and one for the group, a graph of how it connects, and the data as JSON. Up to ten changes included; more at the change rates.
packages.not_included: Anything about a named person that is not already public and professional.
packages.delivered_by: the story-project team (researcher@, ontologist@, dev.pages@, dev.graphs@, journalist@ for the words) with a person's check
needs_before_live: The first delegation done for real (Brazil), so the formula is proven and the price is a fact.

stripe.note: an invoice from the Stripe dashboard to the named buyer; scope sheet attached

needs_before_live: The change policy in operations.md, agreed (what counts as small).

packages.name: Professional services: Starter
packages.buyer: a company that saw our work and asks 'can you do this for us?'

price.basis: Dinis, 6 November 2026: packs of 500, 1,500 or 5,000 pounds of professional services

packages.what: One agentic workflow looked at, written down and shown working once: what it does, what it may do, what stands in the way, and a first running version, in a week.
packages.not_included: Running it for them afterwards; work on their private systems without their written grant.
packages.delivered_by: the partner named on the pack, with this team's agents; a person signs it off
needs_before_live: The partners' own offers written down by them (Dinis named three people who want to sell professional services); this role will not invent their scope.
Who contracts: which legal entity invoices (open question for Dinis).

packages.name: Professional services: Team

needs_before_live: As C1.

packages.what: The method in a room: roles, policies that survive compaction, passes, budgets, hold.
needs_before_live: A person's diary. Not an agent job.

packages.name: Match your list to the graph

The public data's licence: what we publish is public, so the paid part is the match and the hand-holding, never the data.

packages.not_included: Anything private; any promise of coverage; any RiskMandate pitch (not before Dinis says).

packages.what: What happened for them: the sessions they were part of or missed, who spoke on their field, the announcements about their companies, a follow-up list and the source for each, with the data as JSON and a graph.

packages.buyer: a company or investor who wants the field watched after the summit

packages.what: A monthly brief on one field with the changes since last time, sourced.
needs_before_live: Demand after the summit; a person who owns the relationship.

packages.name: Advertising and sponsored placements
packages.why: Dinis, 6 November 2026: 'We have no ads', the space is for the data. Newsletter sponsorship is a real market (see benchmarks), but it would put a buyer's interest beside our judgement on every page. Reopen only on Dinis's word.

packages.name: Paying for an article, a ranking or a removal of a fact
packages.why: The editors, not RiskMandate and not a buyer, decide what is published (content/riskmandate.md). A company can buy a service made for it (B, C, D, E); it can never buy what the publication says. Say so on the page that offers any of this.

packages.name: Selling who reads what
packages.why: Privacy first: no cookies, no tracking, no selling of the user (Dinis, 6 November 2026). Counts only are published.

packages.name: A paywall
packages.why: The meter never blocks a page (data/billing/prices.json, rules). A paywall would break the thing the meter is there to show.
